title: Explore instance-based (per-match) constraint waivers
description:
Waivers today scope to (constraint, file) or at finest (constraint, file, symbol_qualified_name) — the `sutra_constraints action=waive` API exposes only `file_path` and optional `symbol_qualified_name`, with no line or content anchor. This makes waivers too coarse for `forbidden_pattern` rules that legitimately match many times per file/symbol.

Concrete motivating case (vidya adoption): `no-clone-driven-dev` is blocking with 95 pre-existing production matches, all triaged as owned-required (not borrow-bypass). We want them off the `violations`/review report as examined-legit, but the only way is a file- or symbol-level waiver — which ALSO suppresses any *future* clone introduced in that file/symbol, blinding the rule where it's needed. So the current choice is binary: live with the noise, or blind the rule. Neither is right.

Note the introduced-only guard already grandfathers pre-existing matches at *edit* time (by content diff, no waiver needed). The gap is purely in the *reporting* surface (`sutra_constraints violations`, `sutra_review`): no way to mark a specific match instance as "reviewed & accepted" without a scope that also swallows future instances.

Explore: a per-instance / per-match waiver anchored to match content (e.g. a content hash of the matched node + surrounding context, or line+snippet fingerprint that survives reformatting) so a single clone site can be acknowledged while its siblings and any future additions stay governed. Design questions: what anchor is stable across edits/reformatting but specific enough not to collide; how it degrades when the anchored line moves or the file is refactored; whether it unifies with how the introduced-only guard already fingerprints pre-existing matches (likely shared machinery); reporting UX for bulk-acknowledging N examined instances at once.

acceptance_criteria.text: Design note comparing anchor strategies (content-hash vs line+snippet fingerprint vs AST-node identity) with stability-vs-specificity tradeoffs
Decision on whether per-instance waivers share the introduced-only guard's existing match-fingerprinting machinery
Migration/UX story for bulk-acknowledging many examined instances (e.g. the 95 vidya clones) without per-call tedium

decisions.decision: Report-only instance acknowledgments, not guard-honored waivers
decisions.rationale: The gap is purely the reporting surface (sutra_constraints violations, sutra_review, orient) — the guard already grandfathers pre-existing matches via its own proposed-vs-disk introduced-only diff. Keeping acks out of the guard path structurally prevents the file-waiver failure mode where waivers::partition (find_waiver returns true for symbol=None) blinds edit-time enforcement for the whole file.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Content-keyed WAIVER honored by both surfaces — but the guard partitions waived findings out before its introduced-only diff, so a content-keyed waiver would silently allow byte-identical future clones at edit time. Report-only avoids the coupling.

decisions.decision: Content fingerprint anchor = the guard's existing MatchKey (constraint_id, enclosing_symbol, snippet), count-aware
decisions.rationale: snippet is the matched node's first line verbatim, node-relative (excludes leading indentation) — stable across line moves and re-indentation, the common edits. Count-aware (accepted_count) is what keeps future/extra byte-identical siblings governed: baseline count 1, disk count 2 -> 1 surplus reported. Reuses machinery already computed on both sides; zero new fingerprinting.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Line+snippet (brittle — any insertion above shifts the line, waiver goes stale, noise returns; needs fuzzy re-anchoring) and AST-node identity (no durable node id — files.id is re-minted every reparse per sutra/297).

decisions.decision: Separate constraint_instance_acks table, not an extension of constraint_waivers
decisions.rationale: Different semantics (report-only vs guard-honored), different key (content multiset+count vs scope), different reconciliation. Overloading find_waiver/ConstraintWaiverRow would entangle the guard-coupling we are deliberately avoiding.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Add report_only flag + count + key columns to constraint_waivers — rejected to keep find_waiver and the guard path untouched.

implementation_plan:
## Types-first gate

This adds a non-trivial new unit (table + row type + shared MatchKey helper + MCP actions). Suggest running `vidhi-types-first` on the data model (ConstraintInstanceAckRow, MatchKey/subtract_multiset signatures, the `ack`/`baseline`/`unack` arg shape) before implementing. Josh decides.

## Approach

Ship **report-only, count-aware, content-keyed instance acknowledgments** that share the guard's `MatchKey`. Two entry points — `baseline` (bulk snapshot, the vidya-95 answer) and `ack` (single instance + rationale). Acks are subtracted from findings ONLY on the report path (violations / review / orient), never on the guard path, so edit-time introduced-only enforcement stays intact. The high-churn idiomatic-Arc noise is handled out-of-band by the `clone_on_ref_ptr` convention (vidhi/13); this feature handles the residual genuine value-clone judgment calls, which are small and slow-changing.

## Files

- **Create**: `migrations/0058_constraint_instance_acks.sql` — table + unique index (mirror the COALESCE-expression unique index the constraint_waivers ON CONFLICT relies on).
- **Modify**: `src/db/migrations.rs` (~line 290) — register 0058 after 0057.
- **Modify**: `src/db/constraints.rs` — add `ConstraintInstanceAckRow`, `create_constraint_instance_ack` (upsert, count-aware), `get_constraint_instance_acks_for_file`, `delete_constraint_instance_ack`, `reconcile_orphaned_constraint_instance_acks` (mirror `reconcile_orphaned_constraint_waivers`).
- **Modify**: `src/constraints/patterns.rs` — extract the shared `MatchKey` type + `match_key(&ConstraintFinding)` + `subtract_multiset(findings, prior) -> surplus` (lifted verbatim from guard.rs:803-828 so the guard's behavior is byte-preserved).
- **Modify**: `src/guard.rs` — `check_proposed_patterns` calls the extracted `subtract_multiset` instead of its inline loop (behavior unchanged; refactor-contract: multiset cancel, waived excluded from BOTH counts).
- **Modify**: `src/constraints/check.rs` — in `evaluate`, after the waiver partition, subtract instance-acks from the surviving `forbidden_pattern` active findings (count-aware). This is the single chokepoint the report surfaces share.
- **Modify**: `src/tools/constraints.rs` — add `baseline`, `ack`, `unack` actions + args (`line`/`snippet`/`scope`); extend `finding_to_json`/output to report `acknowledged` counts.
- **Test**: `src/guard.rs` #[cfg(test)] (ack does NOT change guard behavior), `src/constraints/check.rs` or `tests/review-test.rs` (report subtraction, count-aware surplus), `tests/db-test.rs` (CRUD + reconcile), `src/tools/constraints.rs` #[cfg(test)] (baseline/ack/unack).

## Steps

### Step 1: Schema + row type

`migrations/0058_constraint_instance_acks.sql`:
```sql
CREATE TABLE constraint_instance_acks (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  constraint_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  constraint_name TEXT,
  file_path       TEXT NOT NULL,
  enclosing_symbol TEXT,          -- MatchKey part (nullable)
  snippet          TEXT,          -- MatchKey part (nullable)
  accepted_count  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  rationale       TEXT,           -- nullable: bulk baseline may omit
  acked_by        TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  updated_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_instance_acks_key ON constraint_instance_acks(
  constraint_id, file_path, COALESCE(enclosing_symbol,''), COALESCE(snippet,''));
```
Register in `migrations.rs` as `0058_constraint_instance_acks`.

```rust
pub struct ConstraintInstanceAckRow {
    pub id: i64,
    pub constraint_id: Arc<str>,
    pub constraint_name: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub file_path: String,
    pub enclosing_symbol: Option<String>,
    pub snippet: Option<String>,
    pub accepted_count: i64,
    pub rationale: Option<String>,
    pub acked_by: String,
    pub created_at: String,
    pub updated_at: String,
}
```

### Step 2: Extract the shared multiset primitive

Lift from guard.rs:803-828 into `patterns.rs` (where findings are born). Verbatim semantics — this is the refactor-contract-sensitive step:
```rust
pub type MatchKey = (Arc<str>, Option<String>, Option<String>);
pub fn match_key(f: &ConstraintFinding) -> MatchKey {
    (f.constraint_id.clone(), f.enclosing_symbol.clone(), f.snippet.clone())
}
/// Cancel one `prior[key]` count per finding sharing that key; return the surplus.
pub fn subtract_multiset(findings: Vec<ConstraintFinding>, prior: &HashMap<MatchKey, usize>) -> Vec<ConstraintFinding> { /* the existing loop */ }
```
Rewrite `check_proposed_patterns` to build `prior` from `disk_active` and call `subtract_multiset`. Guard test suite must stay green unchanged.

### Step 3: DB CRUD + reconcile

`create_constraint_instance_ack(constraint_id, name, file_path, enclosing_symbol, snippet, accepted_count, rationale, acked_by)` — upsert on the unique key, `DO UPDATE SET accepted_count = ?, rationale = COALESCE(?, rationale), updated_at = now`. `get_constraint_instance_acks_for_file(file_path)`. `delete_constraint_instance_ack(id)`. `reconcile_orphaned_constraint_instance_acks` mirrors the waiver version (drop rows whose constraint_id no longer exists).

### Step 4: Report-side subtraction (the chokepoint)

In `check::evaluate`, after the existing waiver partition, for `forbidden_pattern` active findings only:
```rust
let acks = db.get_constraint_instance_acks_for_file(path)?; // per file in scope
let mut prior: HashMap<MatchKey, usize> = HashMap::new();
for a in &acks { *prior.entry((a.constraint_id.clone(), a.enclosing_symbol.clone(), a.snippet.clone())).or_default() += a.accepted_count as usize; }
let active = subtract_multiset(active_patterns, &prior); // surplus reported
```
**Verify routing (do not assume):** confirm `sutra_review` (build_findings) and `orient` produce pattern findings *through* `check::evaluate`. If either runs `check_forbidden_patterns` on its own path, apply the same subtraction there. Grep both before wiring.

### Step 5: MCP actions

`ConstraintsArgs` gains `line: Option<u32>`, `snippet: Option<String>`, `scope: Option<String>`.
- **`baseline`**: resolve constraint (id or name), run `check_forbidden_patterns` over files matching `scope`, group active findings by MatchKey, upsert one ack per key with `accepted_count = group size`. Rationale optional. One call clears the 95.
- **`ack`**: single instance. Resolve the file's findings, select the one at `line` (or matching `snippet`), upsert its key with count 1. Rationale REQUIRED here.
- **`unack`**: delete by id.
Output for `violations` shows `matched: N, acknowledged: M, active: N-M` per (constraint, file) so acks are visible, not silent state.

### Step 6: Tests

- Guard: an ack row does NOT change `check_proposed_patterns` — a new byte-identical clone beyond disk is still denied (guard never reads the ack table).
- Report: 3 acked clones -> 0 active; add a 4th identical (disk count 4, accepted 3) -> 1 surplus reported; a differently-keyed clone always reported.
- Reconcile: orphaned ack (constraint removed / key no longer on disk) stops suppressing (fail-loud) and is GC'd.
- Tool: baseline captures counts; ack requires rationale; unack removes.

## Acceptance criteria coverage

- [x] "Design note comparing anchor strategies with stability-vs-specificity tradeoffs" -> decisions field (content-fingerprint chosen; line+snippet and AST-node-identity rejected with reasons) + Step 2.
- [x] "Decision on whether per-instance waivers share the introduced-only guard's fingerprinting machinery" -> yes, shared via extracted `MatchKey`/`subtract_multiset` (Step 2), but decoupled so acks never touch the guard (decisions field + Step 4 + Step 6 guard test).
- [x] "Migration/UX story for bulk-acknowledging N instances" -> `baseline` action (Step 5), count-aware, one call for the 95; `clone_on_ref_ptr` convention (vidhi/13) removes the high-churn Arc noise so re-baselining stays rare.
execution_record:
Implemented per the plan, no divergence in approach. Content-fingerprint anchor chosen (guard's MatchKey = constraint_id+enclosing_symbol+snippet), shared via extracted patterns::{MatchKey, match_key, subtract_multiset}; guard.rs rewritten onto the shared primitive with byte-preserved behavior. Report subtraction lives only in evaluate_dd (both return points); the guard's RawConn/evaluate_raw path is untouched, so acks are structurally report-only. baseline answers the bulk-ack UX (one call per constraint, count-aware); ack is single-instance, rationale-required, and capped at on-disk match count so repeated/stale acks can't over-suppress.

Notable during execution: centralizing match_key into patterns.rs made its 3 owned-key clones newly-introduced under no-clone-driven-dev (they were grandfathered inline in guard.rs). Resolved with a symbol-scoped waiver (waiver_id 148) with owned-required rationale — dogfooding exactly why coarse waivers are acceptable when a whole symbol is legitimately clone-heavy. Avoided an extra clone by taking subtract_multiset's prior by value, and grouped report findings by file via sort-and-run (no from_path clone) to stay clean under the same rule.

Commit e389fb7. Tests: guard decoupling (pattern_ack_does_not_relax_guard), count-aware report subtraction (constraints-test instance_acks_subtract_on_report_count_aware), DB CRUD+reconcile (db-test x3), MCP baseline/ack/unack (tools tests x2). Full suite 1563 passed / 0 failed; clippy clean; fmt clean.

Note: live MCP sutra server still runs the pre-migration binary — the new table/actions ship on next server rebuild/restart.

messages.text:
Review (vidhi-review, e389fb7^..e389fb7): approve with notes. Guard/report decoupling verified structurally (RawConn only at the 2 guard entry points; DdBacked at all 3 report surfaces; apply_instance_acks reachable only from evaluate_dd) and by test (pattern_ack_does_not_relax_guard). subtract_multiset extraction is behavior-byte-preserving. Ran cargo test --lib (811 ok) + db-test/constraints-test (66+58 ok) — all ack tests green.

1 medium finding: acked instances are surfaced ("acknowledged" array) only on sutra_constraints violations, NOT on sutra_review or orient — they vanish from constraint_violations_total with no trace, unlike waivers which ARE surfaced on review. Defeats the audit rationale for choosing report-only over guard-honored. 2 low: rules::load_rules called twice per baseline/ack; get_all_constraint_instance_acks().unwrap_or_default() at constraints.rs:247 swallows a DB error (display-only). Design note: acks credit a count per content-key, do not pin a line — a same-key replacement keeping the count constant isn't re-surfaced on the report; safe because the guard catches introductions at edit time.

edges.note: 305 provides the instance-based waiver needed to retire genuine value-clone file-waivers during the vidhi/13 rollout; vidhi/13's clone_on_ref_ptr convention removes the idiomatic-noise case that would otherwise dominate 305's baseline.
